🔔 SpaceX stock falls as $60B Cursor deal closes 

‼️ SpaceX has completed its $60 billion stock-based acquisition of Anysphere, bringing the Cursor coding platform into its SpaceXAI business as SPCX shares fell during Friday trading. The closing came less than two months after SpaceX signed the merger agreement on June 16. Under its terms, the company valued Anysphere at an implied equity value of $60 billion and agreed to compensate its investors with SpaceX Class A common stock.

🔖 Cursor’s common and preferred shares outstanding immediately before the merger were automatically converted into rights to receive 389,289,254 SpaceX Class A shares, according to the filing.SpaceX based the exchange on the volume-weighted average closing price of its Class A shares over the seven consecutive trading days before the acquisition closed. Rather than setting one fixed share price when the agreement was signed, the structure tied the final share count to SPCX’s recent market value. 

🌐 Vested Cursor restricted stock units were separately converted into rights to receive 1,752,426 SpaceX Class A shares before applicable tax deductions. Holders will receive cash instead of fractional shares where the exchange calculation does not produce a whole share. Unvested awards will remain tied to future service and vesting requirements. According to the filing, SpaceX assumed the outstanding awards and converted them into about 29,128,326 restricted stock units linked to its Class A shares.

💵⚔️ Economic D-Day: Victory Speech, Then a Call for Help

At 2:11 a.m., Donald Trump announced what he called “the MOST CRUSHING ECONOMIC OPERATION EVER TAKEN AGAINST ANY COUNTRY.”

Iran, he wrote, had no navy, a destroyed air force, military factories in ruins, a worthless currency, and a country “hanging by a thread.”

Then he asked every U.S. ally to help defeat it.

“We need ALL of our Allies to stand with the United States of America to isolate, and defeat, the Iran threat,” Trump wrote. A country said to be on the edge of collapse still requires a coalition to isolate it. 

The warning that followed was aimed less at Tehran than at the governments and businesses that deal with it. Any country whose banks, firms, airports, or state bodies provide Iran “any type of lifeline” will face “TREMENDOUS Economic Consequences,” Trump said. Oil smuggling, currency swaps, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, and front companies must stop “NOW.” 

D-Day is the name associated with the Allied landings in Normandy in 1944. Trump used it for a sanctions escalation and told Washington’s allies that continued dealings with Iran would come at a cost.

The numbers behind the announcement are less theatrical. Iran’s central-bank governor, Abdolnaser Hemmati, said oil exports had all but stopped. He also said the United States had not released Iran’s frozen funds under the Pakistan-brokered Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, a June agreement that was meant to open a 60-day path toward a broader U.S.-Iran settlement. 

The economic pressure was already in place. Trump declared a campaign to make it broader and harder to evade.

According to Axios, the U.S. military has established a shipping corridor through the southern side of the Strait of Hormuz, near Oman. Fifteen to 20 tankers have been using it each night. U.S. officials said roughly 10 million barrels of oil a day now leave the Gulf through the corridor, about half the prewar volume. The corridor operates under U.S. military protection, including fighter cover against Iranian missiles and drones. 

The decisive test is Dubai.

The UAE Foreign Ministry said all trade, commercial exchanges, and financial transactions with Iran had been halted “until further notice.” In 2024, the UAE supplied about $21 billion in goods to Iran — roughly one-third of Iranian imports, according to trade data cited by the Wall Street Journal. 

But a suspension is a policy. Enforcement means following traders, exchange houses, cargo routes, ship registries, and front companies across a system designed to move money and goods quickly and discreetly. Washington is asking that system to police itself.

Oil prices rose to three-week highs as traders assessed the risk that the U.S.-Iran standoff would continue to disrupt Gulf supplies. 

Trump says Iran is hanging by a thread. His policy depends on convincing every bank, trader, port, and government that the thread is too expensive to hold.

📣 EU to revise MiCA rules in 2027 amid US stablecoin push 

⚠️ European Union officials are preparing to revise the bloc’s MiCA crypto framework in 2027 as foreign stablecoin restrictions and faster U.S. rulemaking expose gaps in the existing regime. The planned revision would examine how MiCA treats stablecoins issued outside the European Union. Current requirements have prevented several foreign issuers from receiving authorization, limiting their access to regulated exchanges across the bloc.

💬 “Reopening the file seems unavoidable at this stage,” an unidentified European diplomat told Euronews.

🔗 The diplomat cited positions taken by European institutions, including the European Central Bank, along with changes in global regulation and digital-asset technology. No final proposal has been published. Any amendment would need to pass through the EU’s legislative process before taking effect. The consultation covers developments that have occurred since MiCA entered into application. Its deadline has been extended to Sept. 30, with crypto issuers, service providers, regulators, central banks and finance ministries invited to respond.
